subject: MLRIT
chapter_title: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

hierarchy.label: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

children.label: 1. Database Fundamentals & Engine Architecture
children.description: Explores file system limitations, three-schema architecture, data abstraction, physical and logical data independence, data models, DDL/DML, and the internal engine architecture comprising query processing, transaction management, and storage engine.

children.label: 2. Conceptual Database Design & ER Modeling
children.description: Covers high-level conceptual modeling, entity sets, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued, derived), relationship sets, mapping cardinalities (1:1, 1:N, M:N), participation constraints (total vs. partial), and keys (super, candidate, primary).

children.label: 3. Advanced ER & Extended ER (EER) Mechanisms
children.description: Details weak entity sets, discriminating attributes, identifying relationships, specialization/generalization hierarchies, top-down vs. bottom-up design, disjoint/overlapping constraints, and total/partial completeness rules.

children.label: 4. Relational Model Foundations & Integrity Constraints
children.description: Examines formal relational structure, relations, tuples, attributes, domains, atomic values, degree, cardinality, domain constraints, entity integrity (non-null primary keys), and referential integrity (foreign keys and cascade actions).

children.label: 5. Logical Database Design (ER-to-Relational Translation)
children.description: Presents systematic reduction algorithms for converting ER/EER diagrams to relational schemas, including strong entity tables, weak entity foreign keys, 1:1 and 1:N foreign key embedding, M:N composite associative tables, multivalued attribute normalization, and specialization representation.

children.label: 6. Relational Querying, Views & Schema Evolution
children.description: Covers formal relational query languages including procedural Relational Algebra (Selection, Projection, Cartesian Product, Set Union/Difference, Join), SQL DDL/DML, and database view definitions, updatability constraints, and physical storage mechanisms.
